newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMPLATS SAYS UNION ACCEPTS WAGE IMPROVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: IMPLATS SAYS UNION ACCEPTS WAGE IMPROVEMENT.

text.p: Impala Platinum Ltd (Implats) said that a deal which ended a week-long strike at its platinum refineries included an improved basic wage offer and striking workers would return to work on Tuesday.
The company said the improved basic wage offer would be funded from a reduction in a proposed employee benefit improvement and will cost the company less than its previous offer to employees.
Implats said in a statement on Tuesday that agreement was reached with the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) on Monday afternoon.
About 400 NUM members -- who have been on strike since August 4 -- returned to work on Tuesday.
Implats said on Monday that production had not been affected because non-striking members of the 1,100-strong workforce had kept the refineries going.
Management's last wage offer was a 10.7 percent increase, against the NUM's last demand of 19.2 percent.
Implats gave no further details of the current settlement and NUM officials were not immediately available for comment.
Implats produced 499,000 ounces of refined platinum in the six months to end-December 1996 and normal output is around a million ounces a year.
